issue_context.title: IPv6SendRA.RouterLifetimeSec being required was not obvious
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**

```
systemd 246 (246)
+PAM +AUDIT -SELINUX +IMA -APPARMOR -SMACK -SYSVINIT +UTMP +LIBCRYPTSETUP +GCRYPT +GNUTLS +ACL +XZ +LZ4 +ZSTD +SECCOMP +BLKID +
ELFUTILS +KMOD -IDN2 -IDN -PCRE2 default-hierarchy=hybrid
```


<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released (non-rc) systemd versions upstream! -->
<!-- See https://github.com/systemd/systemd/releases for the list of most recent releases. -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://systemd.io/CONTRIBUTING#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
Clear Linux

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
**CPU architecture issue was seen on**

Linux yyy 5.9.1-992.native #1 SMP Sat Oct 17 03:04:22 PDT 2020 x86_64 GNU/Linux

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
**Steps to reproduce the problem**

I expected that by the time I had configured prefix delegation and router advertisements that router information would be included with the adverts being sent. Router information is not included unless `RouterLifetimeSec` is set to some value.

In addition, no one on `#systemd` on Freenode could spot the issue.

This existing behavior is ok, and is documented under `IPv6SendRA.RouterLifetimeSec` however, this appears to be hard to spot, and there is possibly a need for a fuller example, or a more obvious call-out in the documentation.

Alternatively splitting on/off from time might also make the issue more prominent/obvious.

In particular the documentation opening sentence under `[IPv6SendRA]` is:

```
The [IPv6SendRA] section contains settings for sending IPv6 Router Advertisements and whether to act as a router, if enabled via the IPv6SendRA= option described above. IPv6 network prefixes or routes are defined with one or more [IPv6Prefix] or [IPv6RoutePrefix] sections.
```

This is misleading in some sense, as it suggests to the reader that enabling this section at all (via `Network.IPv6SendRA`) should start advertising the system as a router, but it does not.

A similar modification may also want to be included under `Network.IPv6SendRA`, as it mentions for example `IPv6RoutePrefix` and other sections, but does not call out the need to set this timeout.

review_comments: I don't think we should do this. UINT_MAX is only ~18h, and we might want to set it larger than than in the future, even if the current underlying implementation does not allow this. So let's instead keep the original interface, and maybe return -ERANGE if appropriate.
But RFC says the router lifetime is 16bit unsigned. We cannot easily extend it in the future. See e.g. [RFC 4191](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4191#section-2.2), or netinet/icmp6.h.

Seems shortsighted — I think it's fine for a field in a packet to be short (since bytes matter there). But using a 16 param in a function call, which is going to be passed as `int` anyway seems like a pointless optimization. But OK, I don't think this matters. If the kernel uses 16 bits, if this is ever changed, it'll need to be changed across the board.
